title: Mapping the global patent landscape of phage therapy
summary: Who patents phage therapy, where, and on which technologies: a global landscape from 1955 to 2023.
problem: Phage therapy is a fast-growing alternative to antibiotics, but nobody had mapped who patents it, where, and on what.
approach: Collected 5,753 patents, merged them into 2,365 patent families, found 10 technology themes with topic modelling, and measured applicant and inventor impact in Python.
result: First-author article in Nature Biotechnology (December 2024), with all code public.
contribution: First author: study design, patent collection and cleaning, NLP, network analysis and writing.
outputs: 2,365 patent families; figures, networks, topic models; Nature Biotechnology article

title: A harmonised global dataset of preprints, 1990–2025
summary: One clean record for every preprint, harmonised across Crossref, DataCite and OpenAlex.
problem: Preprint metadata are split across Crossref, DataCite and OpenAlex, with inconsistent server names and duplicate records.
approach: Built harvesters for each source, wrote rules to identify preprint servers, linked versions and removed duplicates.
result: 7,905,699 harvested records reduced to 7,332,492 parent records from 109 servers; dataset paper in preparation for Quantitative Science Studies.
contribution: Lead author and data engineer at ScholCommLab, Simon Fraser University.
outputs: Harmonised dataset; harvesters; manuscript in preparation

title: Open access and research inequalities in Africa
summary: Two decades of African research output, open access and collaboration, measured at continental scale.
problem: Open-access policy for African research is debated with little continent-wide evidence.
approach: Analysed 854,785 articles published 2002–2021 by open-access route, collaboration pattern and funding, using OpenAlex and Unpaywall.
result: Manuscript in preparation. Open articles tended to be more cited, and international collaboration drove access.
contribution: Lead author: data assembly, analysis and writing.

title: Immune-checkpoint therapy patent intelligence

title: COVID-19 research in Africa: output, collaboration and leadership
summary: How much COVID-19 research African scientists led, and with whom they worked.
problem: It was unclear how much COVID-19 research African scientists led, and with whom.
approach: Searched Web of Science, PubMed and African Journals Online, screened and de-duplicated records, and measured authorship and collaboration.
result: First-author article in IJERPH (2021), with the full dataset shared openly.
contribution: First author: search strategy, screening, bibliometric analysis and writing.

title: Exploring the human respiratory microbiota
summary: Doctoral research that grew and described bacteria never isolated before from the human airways.
problem: Most bacteria living in the human respiratory tract had never been grown or described.
approach: Combined culturomics with metagenomics on clinical samples, and wrote a systematic review of every bacterial species reported from the mouth and airways.
result: 35 new bacterial species described, including 5 new genera; PhD defended in November 2018.
contribution: PhD researcher at IHU Méditerranée Infection, Aix-Marseille Université: isolation, characterisation and writing.

title: How science builds, uses and studies generative AI
summary: A screened OpenAlex corpus of generative-AI research since 2020, classified facet by facet with validated LLM coding.
problem: Generative-AI papers are usually counted by keyword, which mixes papers that build models with papers that only mention ChatGPT. There is no reliable picture of how the balance of building, using, evaluating and debating GenAI has shifted since 2022.
approach: Harvested an OpenAlex corpus with GenAI concept and tool terms (2020 onward), screened every title and abstract with LLMs, and wrote a codebook for each classification facet, starting with GenAI's role in the paper, tested against hand-coded records.
result: Facet 1, GenAI's role, agrees with 300 blind hand-coded records at κ 0.89 (91% agreement). More facets, articles on CognosX Insights and a public dashboard are in progress.
contribution: Lead, through CognosX: corpus design, LLM screening and classification pipeline, facet codebooks, hand-coded gold standards and analysis.
outputs: Screened corpus; facet codebooks; validated gold sets; forthcoming articles and dashboard
